items.title: Bill Huntington Interview, 1961-12-27
items.q: I think Emile Barnes had it. The cool attitude.

ctx.x: What did he teach you in, uh, in the very fundamental technical things I'm talking about? Uh, not just, just start at the beginning, before you ever got into anything like harmony, just, how to hold your banjo and how to stroke it.

Yeah, this was very interesting. He taught me, uh, he didn't teach exactly. I sort of observed. Uh, he had a very relaxed, uh, I don't give a damn attitude towards, towards playing. No, that's, that's not the right word. Uh, you know, it's not that he didn't give a damn. He, he, he just, he just kind of, he just kind of realized that, that swinging was a very natural thing. And no amount of foot stomping and, and, uh, uh, exaggerated, uh, exaggerated activity was going to make you swing. It was a very natural…

Well, they were restrained and casual to me. Yeah. Look at guys like that. Yeah. I mean they weren't trying to prove anything to anybody. Right. Exactly. That's what it meant. They felt like stomping their foot, they would.
